item.title: This farm raised thousands of pigs for slaughter. Now it's growing mushrooms instead
item.description: The U.S. gets nearly a third of its pork from Iowa. One family is making the switch from pigs to more sustainable specialty mushrooms and trying to show other pig farmers how they did it.

item.title: How a national farm leader is dealing with record diesel prices
item.description: John Boyd Jr., president of the National Black Farmers Association, says soaring diesel costs are deepening a farm crisis as farmers face sharply higher fuel costs in the middle of harvest season.

item.title: This Minnesota farmer is feeling the pressure of rising gas prices
item.description: NPR's Elissa Nadworny speaks with Kristin Duncanson, a farmer in Minnesota, about how record high fuel prices are affecting her business.

item.title: Energy expert Bob McNally on how to protect consumers from a looming gas price spike
item.description: Analysts are warning about an impending jump in gas prices. NPR's Scott Simon talks with Bob McNally, of Rapidan Energy about how and even if the economic effects can be mitigated.

item.title: Ever wonder how the Fed's interest rate actually works? We've got answers
item.description: The Federal Reserve just raised interest rates this week for the first time this year. So how does it actually work? And what does it mean for the economy — and the rest of us? Here are some answers.

item.title: Diesel prices reach record territory, creating ripple effects throughout the economy
item.description: Diesel prices soared to another record high today, averaging $6.44 a gallon. Trucking, farming, and flying is getting more expensive. But so far it hasn't crimped most Americans' spending.

item.title: Stocks hit records as AI optimism grows, but bond markets tell a different story
item.description: The stock market is at record highs, largely thanks to tech stocks that are benefitting from investor optimism about the AI boom. But bond markets may be telling a different story.
